title: Classes
bridge: A C++ class bundles data and functions: `class Enemy { public: Enemy(std::string n, int hp); void takeDamage(int d); private: int health; };`. Members are `private` by default. A **constructor** has the class's name; the `: name(n), health(hp)` part (an initialiser list) sets the fields. Mark functions that only read with `const`. End the class with `};`.

exercises.title: Enemy
exercises.prompt: Finish class Enemy: a constructor Enemy(std::string name, int health); void takeDamage(int amount) (never below 0); void heal(int amount) (never above the starting health); bool isDead() const; and std::string describe() const, which gives e.g. Goblin (18 HP).

tests.hint_if_fail: Health stops at 0, and 0 means dead.

tests.call: []{ Enemy e("Orc", 20); e.takeDamage(50); e.heal(5); return e.describe(); }()
[]{ Enemy e("Orc", 20); e.takeDamage(5); e.heal(100); return e.describe(); }()
tests.hint_if_fail: Heal never goes above the starting health: keep that in its own field.

hints: Fields: std::string name; int health; int maxHealth;

quiz.q: Class members are ___ by default in C++.
quiz.why: class defaults to private (struct defaults to public).

quiz.q: What does const after a member function mean?

choices: Sets the fields before the constructor body runs

cards.a: A function with the class's name and no return type.

explain: Explain classes to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
